scope: Read-only review of the staged scenario source and new unit fragment against the browser fixture's real workflow assumptions.
confirmedContracts: The stored timed-practical scenario ID remains intact while its display name distinguishes four-minute technique practice from Study identification.
Selection and Start use native non-restart activation. The original active-layer technique and inspection records stay intact.
An unstarted challenge has no countdown. Active and completed timers are separate quiet outputs outside the polite status text.
The displayed expired state overrides a stale positive countdown without rewriting the stored record. Native complete progress retains its frozen remaining-time snapshot.
Expiry recovery comes after existing Study, assessment and Guided priorities. Its action opens the technique panel and focuses Restart without resetting records.

Private owner-scoped restart review state is excluded from saved lab data and cleared with its owner. The scope tracks specimen, layer, scenario, start time, workspace/activity flags, technique revisions, selected-specimen inspection revisions, and revealed state.
Unit stale-confirmation cases invoke the actual mounted React callback. They exercise the callback guard instead of relying on detached DOM event delegation.
Notes are intentionally outside restart revision scope, so a revised note remains available when the user confirms a current valid review.

The native restart resets active-layer technique and all inspected structures for the selected specimen. Other-layer technique, other-specimen inspections, notes, confidence, captured frames, assessment records, and archived attempts are covered by meaningful preservation assertions.
Browser clock cases exercise the real one-second scenario interval and the independent Study identification interval. They complement the unit tests that use mounted controls and a mocked Date.
